subject: SIG follow-up — hosting responsibilities & operational notes for procurement

Subject: SIG: clarification on Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private responsibilities

Hi Markus —

Thanks for the initial SIG packet. Procurement asked for a short, consolidated note that maps who is responsible for what in each hosting mode (Hosted / Dedicated / Private (VPC or on-prem)). The team wants this framed specifically for contract language so we can confirm SLAs, patching cadence, and evidence ownership.

Specifically, could you confirm:
- Who is the custodian of customer data at rest and in transit for each mode?
- Which party owns runtime patching and kernel updates?
- Where do audit logs live and who retains access for incident review?
- Any differences in backup/retention responsibilities for Dedicated vs Private?

If you can attach a single table and a short narrative that we can attach to the SIG response, that would be ideal. Our timeline is tight — procurement review by Thursday PST.

Appreciate it,
Samantha

Subject: Re: SIG: clarification on Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private responsibilities

Hi Samantha —

Thanks — attached is a compact responsibilities table and a short PDF with proposed wording you can drop into the SIG. High-level bullets below; the CSV spells out line-by-line who owns what.

Summary (short):
- Hosted (Redwood-managed): Redwood is the operator of the control plane and inference runtime; we manage OS/kernel patches, runtime updates, and physical/hypervisor security. Customers retain rights and controls over their data; we encrypt data at rest and in transit. Audit logs are stored in a customer-scoped project; access is via role-based controls and can be exported to customer SIEMs on request.
- Dedicated (Reserved capacity in Redwood cloud): Operational ownership is shared. Redwood manages the underlying fleet and scheduled maintenance; customer is responsible for application-level configuration, model artifacts, and any customer-managed encryption keys if chosen. Backup and snapshot schedules are defined in the contract — we recommend quarterly snapshot retention by default, longer retention can be added as a purchase.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): Customer-managed environment. Redwood provides a private control plane or on-prem package; customer owns host patching, network ACLs, and physical access controls. Redwood supports orchestration, provides signed binaries and upgrade windows, and can manage updates under a managed-support add-on. Audit logs can be retained on customer storage; Redwood will provide the log export and schema.

Key call-outs for SIG language:
- "Redwood as operator" applies only to Hosted. For Dedicated we will commit to operational support SLA but the contract should specify boundaries for kernel/host-level emergency patches.
- Encryption: we support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) in Dedicated and Private; in Hosted we offer managed keys by default with an optional KMS integration.
- Evidence: SOC 2 reports / penetration test summaries are provided by Redwood for Hosted and Dedicated. For Private on-prem deployments, evidence is limited to the artifacts Redwood controls (signed code, release notes, and integration test reports); on-prem security controls are provided by the customer and validated during onboarding.

Attachments: redwood-deployment-responsibilities.csv (table that maps each SIG line item to responsible party + sample contract clause), redwood-sig-answers-v1.pdf (narrative + proposed SIG Q answers), deployment-topology-annotated.png (illustrative diagram).

If you want, Laura can run through the contract clause language with procurement before Thursday.

Thanks,

—Markus Klein
